title: The cell cycle and mitosis; Stem cells
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CD01b#t4 term and clue written for the game; CD01b#t3 term and clue written for the game; CD01b#t1 term and clue written for the game; CD01b#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CD01b#N.2, CE08a#N.2, CD01b#N.5, CE08a#N.4b, CE08a#N.8.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Anaphase
items.clue: Two groups of V-shaped chromatids are moving apart

items.label: Metaphase
items.clue: Chromosomes lie in a single line across the equator

items.label: Interphase
items.clue: Intact nucleus with no separate chromosomes visible; the look of most cells

items.label: Prophase
items.clue: Thread-like chromosomes lie scattered while the nuclear envelope disappears

questions.stem: Two cells are seen in a stained micrograph of a root tip. Cell 1 has an intact nucleus in which no separate chromosomes can be distinguished. Cell 2 has no nuclear envelope, and its condensed chromosomes lie in a single line across the middle of the cell. Which identification is correct?

options.text: Cell 1 is in prophase; cell 2 is in metaphase.
Cell 1 is in interphase; cell 2 is in prophase.
Cell 1 is in interphase; cell 2 is in metaphase.
Cell 1 is in interphase; cell 2 is in early anaphase.

questions.explanation: An intact nucleus with no distinct chromosomes is a cell between divisions. Condensed chromosomes aligned at the equator, envelope gone, is metaphase.

questions.stem: Which pair of properties defines a stem cell?

options.text: Capacity to divide endlessly and ability to differentiate along different pathways.
Ability to divide whenever a tissue is damaged and to produce more cells of its own type.
Ability to switch from one specialised type to another whenever a tissue requires this.
Continuous division at all times, giving new cells whether or not they are needed.

questions.explanation: A stem cell can divide endlessly, and it can differentiate along different pathways to give specialised cell types. Both are required.

questions.stem: In a stained root-tip squash, one cell shows two groups of V-shaped chromatids, their points facing opposite ends of the cell. Which explains this appearance?

options.text: The chromatids are repelling each other and drifting apart; the V shape is the drag of the cytoplasm.
Homologous chromosomes are being separated, each bent at the middle where it was paired.
It is anaphase: spindle fibres attached at each centromere pull it towards a pole, so the arms trail behind.
It is anaphase: the spindle fibres contract like muscle fibres, folding each chromatid in half.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes pluripotent stem cells from totipotent stem cells?

options.text: Pluripotent and totipotent cells can both form every cell type, so the two terms are interchangeable.
Pluripotent cells can form any cell type of the body but not extra-embryonic tissues such as the placenta.
Pluripotent cells are the stem cells found in adult tissues such as bone marrow and hair follicles.
Pluripotent cells appear only after birth, since all the cells of an embryo remain totipotent.

questions.explanation: Totipotent cells of the very early embryo can form every cell, including the placenta and membranes. Within a few divisions the cells become pluripotent: they can still form any body cell type but not the extra-embryonic tissues.

questions.stem: A cell is taken from adult bone marrow and grown in a dish. It divides many times. Some daughter cells stay like the parent; others become erythrocytes, neutrophils and other blood cells, but never nerve or muscle cells. Which statement is correct?

options.text: It cannot be a stem cell, because a stem cell can form every type of body cell.
It is a specialised blood cell that divides whenever more blood is needed.
It is a stem cell, though it can form only a limited range of cell types.
It has lost the genes for nerve and muscle proteins, so it can make only blood cells.

questions.explanation: It divides repeatedly, keeps a population like itself, and differentiates. But only into blood cells, not every body cell.
